reason: The plan shows no feature that survives in the imagery: the drawn defences, moat and lower town lie under ploughed fields with no mark, the excavated structures are not visible, and the mound's visible outline is a cadastral boundary that cannot be matched to the plan's contours. Fewer than three usable features.

candidates_considered.feature: outer (pre-Harappan / Indus) fortification rectangle and its corner bastions
candidates_considered.why: its line lies 60-80 m outside the protected mound under ploughed fields of the cadastral grid; no soil or crop mark in any of the four captures

candidates_considered.feature: Harappan defence wall of the acropolis (black, curving north-west to south)
candidates_considered.why: no wall, trench or ridge visible; a perimeter foot track curves through the same part of the mound but continues right round it, so it cannot be identified with the wall

candidates_considered.feature: curved pre-Harappan acropolis wall and the BB drain ramp
excavated structures on the east side (drains, steps, entrance, post-Harappan structures, well)
candidates_considered.why: backfilled or eroded; the only structures on the mound are a small modern shelter and a modern building on the north-east margin, neither drawn on the plan
no trace; the one open trench (2012 capture, north-west quarter) is later than the plan and not drawn on it

the mound's visible edge is the protected-land boundary, three sides of which are straight field lines; its corners are cadastral corners, and the shape does not match the contours, so no contour bend can be identified

candidates_considered.feature: bank of the dry bed of the Sarasvati, about 150-200 m south-west
candidates_considered.why: fields of the regular grid; no channel edge visible

candidates_considered.feature: pre-Harappan structures inside the acropolis (west side)
auxiliary plan of Banawali in the same publications
candidates_considered.why: the other figures with images in the Banawali entries of IAR 1983-84 and 1987-88 are pottery plates, a fire altar and sections; none is a plan showing surviving features

notes: The site was found at the published coordinates: a fenced, tree-lined protected mound about 213 m east-west and 270 m north-south, 400 m south of Banawali village, inside a regular grid of irrigated fields. Current imagery (Vantor Vivid 20230508) has no zoom-19 tiles; six releases were compared (2012, 2021, 2023 captures; dates from the Wayback metadata layers, read as month/day/year). The mound surface shows only foot tracks, a small modern shelter, a modern building on the north-east margin and, in the 2012 capture only, a fresh rectangular trench in the north-west quarter that the plan does not draw. The mound's outline is the boundary of the protected land: its north, east and west sides are straight field lines of the cadastral grid, and its two diagonal sides do not follow the plan's rectilinear fortification or the shape of its 209-210 m contours. Everything the plan draws outside that boundary (the pre-Harappan and Harappan defences, the moat, the lower town, the bank of the dry bed) lies under ploughed fields with no soil or crop mark. Orientation statements seen while checking the publications for an auxiliary plan: the text extract of iar_198384ar.pdf page index 33 begins with a sentence describing the course of the wall exposed in Tr OC by compass points (a qualitative direction), and the section drawing on iar_198788ar.pdf page index 31 is labelled with compass points at its two ends; I stopped reading at each. Seen without opening any file: the session's starting git status, and a later `git status` run to confirm which files I had written, list untracked conjecture files whose names state working hypotheses about town orientation (knowledge/conjectures/C-0015-towns-laid-out-on-star-settings.md and C-0016-plains-cities-on-true-north.md). They give no value for any plan, and I chose no point with them in mind.
